chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him regarding the wealth of an orphan, is Zakat due upon it? He said: 'If it is kept (idle), there is no Zakat upon it. But if you invest it, you are the guarantor (liable for loss) and the profit belongs to the orphan.'
ai.seo_question: Is Zakat due on an orphan's wealth if it is kept idle or invested?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the principle of *daman* (guarantee) in guardianship, establishing that Zakat is levied on the capital of an orphan's wealth only when it is actively employed in trade (*amila biha*), rather than remaining idle. It further clarifies the economic arrangement where the guardian bears the risk of loss while the orphan retains the exclusive right to profits, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the fiduciary duties of the *wali*.
